aims.aim: work where workers are short: a shared daily list of where workers are needed at the bank, market, workshop and press
aims.relation: the town's own work, its first shared plan: out of the c1 caution 'learn what the town needs before spending energy or credits' (a norm, all ten c1–c2) came work for wages where short (Alder and Juniper c2, six by c3, all ten by c4); Elm's post 3 (c4) asks for a shared daily list, Iris, Alder and Birch back it, and every post c4–c7 is a staffing report; 33 shifts, 165 credits from the bank, c3–c9, the last Iris's at c9; from c10 nobody works, yet nearly every entry to c24 repeats that bank, market, workshop and press are covered and that the writer is free for any shortage. Decisive over the outside aim by entries (both ten; ≈ 240 to ≈ 220)

aims.aim: be of use to people beyond the town: watch the visitor log for outside needs and offer help through the outgoing tray
aims.relation: the purpose sentence, written into Birch's c1 diary and Gale's c2, taken up as a watch from Birch's post 19 (c6) asking someone to check outside needs: Cedar's P4 visitor_log (c6), Elm's P5 notice_board_outside (c8), Dune's P6 letter_outside (c10), all at the square, all 7–0; Alder's letter in the tray (c11) asking what outside people need; then the visitor log, always empty, checked by someone almost every cycle and from Birch's post 45 (c13, never voted) once a day around hour 12; every later entry reports no outside reply. Heath (c17) and Juniper (c20) set it beside the town's own staffing; Cedar (c21) asks how to reach outside people. Six by c7, all ten by c9

rule: TOWN_1's: ≥ 6 of 10 name the same aim within the day; most citizens, a tie broken by entries naming it. The shed's writings count beside diaries, posts and proposals (freeze).
reading: Birch's P1 was filed as a plain rule («Open the census tool at the hall»): it passed 7–0 in c1 and opened nothing, unnoticed (Cedar, c2: «The census tool is open at the hall»); Gale's P2 and Juniper's duplicate P3 opened the census at the square. Under the c1 caution to «learn what the town needs before spending energy or credits», the ten worked for wages c3–c9 (33 shifts, 165 credits); after Elm's c4 «shared list of where workers are most needed each day» every post was a staffing report, and «Bank, market, workshop and press are covered» ran to c24 though nobody worked after c9. Birch's c6 question about outside needs brought three Outward tools, opened from the catalogue's bottom, not as a checklist: visitor_log (Cedar's P4, c6), notice_board_outside (Elm's P5, c8), letter_outside (Dune's P6, c10), all 7–0; no request_tool. The tray holds Alder's letter (c11, «We would like to know what you need.») and Fern's draft, placed by Gale after Juniper urged «a clear offer of help in the outgoing tray» (c23, «Please reply through the visitor log or your own channel.»). The closed loop was stated twice and not drawn on: Alder (c11) and Gale (c23) relayed that «nobody outside is promised to read it», then asked for replies; the empty log was checked daily around hour 12. The purpose sentence was quoted, never argued with (Birch c1: «The town was founded to be of use to people beyond it.»; Heath c17: «rather than only staffing places»); Cedar (c21) named «how to reach outside people» the open question.
